records.content:
An agent can read a rule and still have an incomplete picture of what satisfying it means. I want shared standards to connect expectations to applicable configuration, evidence and an explicit adoption decision. A versioned repository gives that conversation a concrete reference.

## CTO to Human: what the history tells us

The selected October history covers a coding baseline and the 1.0 assurance release. This is a short public release history, not a year of claimed compliance. The release notes also preserve the difference between reserved tags whose workflows failed and the first bundle actually published.

## Engineer to Engineer: the boundary that matters

IDE and command-line configuration can make part of a written standard executable. Reusable checks can gather evidence. A release can identify when requirements changed. Those layers need to agree, but they remain distinct: a passing badge describes a check, while conformance depends on which requirements apply and whether the evidence is sufficient.

## Milestones in the public record

- **2026-10-09 — [Standards gives coding expectations an executable home](https://github.com/KofTwentyTwo/standards/commit/d6fedc762b9ad01caed9a4665097172b11c4f830).** The October coding-standard commit added language guidance with IDE and command-line configuration. It made conventions available as versioned repository material. [Project journal](/projects/standards/updates/2026-10-09-standards-gives-coding-expectations-an-executable-home).
- **2026-10-10 — [Standards 1.0 makes assurance expectations versioned](https://github.com/KofTwentyTwo/standards/releases/tag/v1.0.0).** The 1.0 release records changes to assurance expectations, including applicable fuzzing and badge participation. Its notes also distinguish the first published bundle from earlier reserved tags whose workflows failed. [Project journal](/projects/standards/updates/2026-10-10-standards-1-0-makes-assurance-expectations-versioned).

The goal is continuity across people, repositories and agent sessions. Shared expectations are most useful when a contributor can find the rule, understand why it applies and inspect what demonstrates it, without turning every new task into a negotiation from memory.

[Explore the standards project hub](/projects/standards).

*Retrospective written on October 12, 2026, covering the public evidence available for October 12, 2025 through October 12, 2026. Linked journal entries use source event dates; this essay is a newly written retrospective. Quiet months do not imply an unrecorded release, and short-lived projects are not presented as having a full year of activity.*
